Julius Caesar was a central figure in the Roman Republic, which transitioned into the Roman Empire during his lifetime and shortly after his assassination. While he held the title of dictator for life, he did not rule as an emperor; the Roman Empire was formally established by his adopted heir, Augustus. Therefore, the political entity associated with his rule is the Roman Republic, though he is often credited with paving the way for the Roman Empire.

Regarding the crepe recipe provided, the preparation involves whisking eggs, milk, flour, salt, and melted butter, which typically takes about 5 minutes. The cooking process involves heating a pan and cooking each crepe for approximately 1 minute per side (2 minutes total per crepe). Since the recipe yields enough batter for multiple crepes (using 1 cup of flour and 1 cup of milk), and assuming a standard batch of 4-6 crepes, the cooking time would be roughly 8-12 minutes. Adding the time to heat the pan (about 2-3 minutes), the total estimated preparation and cooking time is approximately 15 to 20 minutes.
